checklist.claim: With an empty filter, 'showing 183 of 183' checks that the meta denominator is row_count (N), not M.

phase3_findings.description: No changelog.d/351.<category>.md fragment for a user-visible change (AGENTS.md Release & distribution).
No release-note fragment for a user-visible change; changelog.d has no 351.*.md.
When _compute_table_payload raises, the agent gets no display line while the user sees 'could not be displayed' — divergent signals (AC13 mandates no display line on this path).
'Too large to show as a table' display line has no matching system-prompt instruction.
row_cap_of drops a malformed cap without logging.
row_cap_marker_data does not validate the cap; cap_size 0 (TRUNCATED_ATTR without MAX_ROWS_ATTR) silently suppresses every user-facing cap notice.
Table payload is an untyped dict; suggest TablePayload TypedDict.
_format.py imports six private names from _table_payload.py.
row_cap_of invalid-value handling untested.
Widget row_cap validation untested.
CSV warning with both truncated>0 and rowCap>0 untested.
Cap hit with no MAX_ROWS_ATTR (cap_size 0) silently drops the cap signal; untested.
Prompt test asserts literal wording rather than behavior.
Weak '_' check in uncut-table test.
test_output_boundaries stubs csvCutWarning, bypassing the real function.
Prompt says never make row-limit statements about schema lookups, but truncation_note is appended for schema lookups too.
run_sql_display_line docstring 'its N is the block's row_count' imprecise when the formatter later drops the block.
Moved _ACRONYMS comment is provenance, not prevention.
Prompt row-limit wording ('stopped at the row limit') does not match the note the agent receives ('Result truncated at N rows').
Size search runs twice per cut table.
'1 rows' grammar when M == 1.
